title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Chen
body:
Purpose and scope

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management & retention, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, contractors, and partners who perform operational, engineering, finance, security, or people-ops responsibilities.

Owners and contacts

- Policy owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com)
- Security owner (vendor/data controls): Security & Compliance (security@redwood.com)
- Procurement and travel: Finance (procurement@redwood.com, travel@redwood.com)
- Change & infra approvals: Eng SRE (sre-oncall@redwood.com)

Summary of sections

1) Access & permissions
2) Change management
3) Data management and retention
4) Procurement and expenses
5) Vendor management and onboarding
6) Travel policy and expense templates
7) Internal templates and where to find them

1) Access & permissions

Goal: enforce least-privilege access, timely onboarding/offboarding, and auditable authorization decisions.

Key principles:
- Principle of least privilege: grant only the minimum permissions required for role tasks.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) mapped to job roles.
- Two-person approval for any privileged (admin) access.
- MFA required for all human accounts.
- Service accounts: rotate keys quarterly and follow the service-account lifecycle process below.

Role definitions (examples):
- employee: base network, single sign-on (SSO), read access to internal wiki and documentation.
- engineer: employee + repo read (and write where needed), cloud console access scoped to project.
- infra-admin: elevated cloud permissions; limited to named individuals with approval.
- finance: access to billing/expense systems only.

Onboarding procedure (1-7 business days goal):
1. Manager submits Onboarding Access Request (OAR) in the HR portal with role and resource list.
2. People Ops reviews and assigns standard role groups.
3. Security verifies any elevated requests (admin roles, production DB access).
4. SSO account provisioned; MFA enforced; initial training checklist completed.
5. Owner confirms access after 48 hours.

Offboarding procedure (24-hour SLA for termination):
1. People Ops triggers automated offboarding workflow on termination/completion.
2. All SSO sessions revoked, device access blocked, tokens/keys scheduled for rotation.
3. Manager confirms handover of work and secrets.
4. Security performs an access audit within 48 hours.

Privileged access approval matrix:
- Any admin/cloud-owner access: manager + security approval required.
- Database superuser: manager + security + infra-owner approval.
- Production deploy permissions: manager + on-call SRE approval.

Service account lifecycle (table):
Step | Owner | SLA | Notes
----- | ----- | --- | -----
Request | Service owner | 2 business days | Request via internal service-account form
Approval | Security + Infra | 3 business days | Approve scope, rotation policy
Creation | Infra | 1 business day | Create with least privilege roles
Rotation | Service owner | Quarterly | Automated rotation using Secrets Manager

2) Change management

Purpose: ensure operational stability and predictable deployment of changes with clear ownership and rollback plans. Applies to infra, runtime, model-serving configs, and database schema changes.

Change types and approval flow:
- Standard change (non-disruptive): documented, auto-approved via ticketing if falls within runbook safe parameters.
- Minor change (may impact performance): manager + owner approval; deploy in maintenance window.
- Major change (risk of downtime or customer impact): CAB approval required; must include rollback plan and test plan.
- Emergency change: follow emergency CAB process; post-facto review required within 3 business days.

Scheduled maintenance windows:
- Weekly: Saturday 02:00-04:00 UTC for low-risk infra tasks.
- High-impact upgrades require 2-week customer and internal notice.

Change request template (must be attached to ticketing):
1. Change title and owner
2. Summary and purpose
3. Systems/components affected
4. Risk assessment (low/medium/high)
5. Rollback plan and verification steps
6. Proposed schedule and maintenance window
7. Approvals (list approvers and timestamps)

Emergency change process:
1. Pager duty escalation to on-call SRE.
2. Owner documents change in ticketing system with reason and immediate approvals (on-call + manager).
3. Execute change and run verification steps.
4. Postmortem and retrospective created within 72 hours.

3) Data management and retention

Classification levels:
- Public: safe to publish externally. Retention: as business needs.
- Internal: company-internal information. Retention: 3 years default.
- Confidential: customer PII, contractual info. Retention: 7 years or per contract.
- Restricted: regulated personal data / PHI / financial records. Retention: per law/contract (may exceed 7 years).

Handling rules:
- All confidential and restricted data must be encrypted at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Use pseudonymization where possible; avoid storing raw PII unless required.
- Access to confidential/restricted data requires documented business justification and Security approval.

Retention and deletion:
- Data retention schedules are defined per dataset. Owners must publish retention for each dataset in the Data Catalog.
- Deletion requests: People Ops and Security coordinate for employee data; customer deletion per contract and privacy policy. Target: complete deletions within 30 days unless legal hold applies.

Backups and recovery:
- Critical production datastore backups: daily snapshots retained 30 days, weekly snapshots retained 90 days, monthly snapshots retained 2 years.
- Recovery RTO: 4 hours for critical systems; RPO: 1 hour for critical DBs.

Data access review cadence:
- Quarterly audit of privileged access to datasets classified confidential or higher.
- Any anomalous access triggers immediate incident investigation.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
- <= $2,500: manager approval.
- $2,501-25,000: manager + finance approval.
- > $25,000: manager + finance + executive sponsor.
- Annual vendor contracts: finance review required for any recurring spend.

Purchase process (3-14 business days depending on vendor):
1. Submit Purchase Request in procurement system with justification and budget code.
2. Finance validates budget and routing.
3. Vendor onboarding (see Vendor section) if contract required.
4. PO issued by Finance.

Expense policy highlights:
- Travel: employees must use company travel portal unless pre-approved exceptions.
- Per-diem: $75/day domestic; $125/day international (or actuals with receipts).
- Meal limits: $60 per meal domestic; $90 international.
- Non-reimbursable: alcohol without business purpose, fines, personal leisure upgrades without approval.

Reimbursement timeline: submit expenses within 30 days; Finance processes within 10 business days after submission with complete receipts.

5) Vendor management and onboarding

Goals: ensure vendor risk is understood and mitigated before any data or production access is granted.

Vendor risk tiers:
- Tier 1 (High): vendors with access to customer data or production systems. Requires SOC2/ISO27001 evidence and security review.
- Tier 2 (Medium): vendors with internal data access; require security questionnaire and contract security clauses.
- Tier 3 (Low): public SaaS with no access to internal or customer data; standard procurement onboarding.

Onboarding checklist (target 5-15 business days):
1. Business owner submits Vendor Request Form with SOW, budget, and data access needs.
2. Finance confirms spend classification.
3. Security runs vendor questionnaire and reviews certifications.
4. Legal reviews contract and required clauses (data processing addendum, liability & indemnity, termination rights).
5. Insurance verification (minimum $1M general liability for Tier 1).
6. Technical onboarding: create service accounts with limited scope, rotate keys, monitor via logs.

Contract & security requirements (examples):
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA) required for any vendor processing customer personal data.
- Right to audit clause for Tier 1 vendors.
- Breach notification timeline: vendor must notify Redwood within 72 hours of any security breach.

Offboarding vendors:
- Revoke all access, collect assets, and validate data deletion per DPA. Completion target: 10 business days.

6) Travel policy & emergency procedures

Booking and approvals:
- Book travel through the company travel portal to ensure corporate rates and insurance.
- All travel over $1,500 estimated cost requires manager approval.
- International travel to high-risk geographies requires Security pre-clearance and registered itinerary.

Per-diem and lodging:
- Use mid-tier hotels; upgrades require manager pre-approval.
- Receipts required for reimbursement.

Safety and incident reporting:
- In emergency or evacuation scenarios, contact Global Security (security@redwood.com) and People Ops immediately.
- File incident report in the Incident system within 48 hours.

7) Internal templates and canonical links

Common templates (location: Internal Templates page):
- Access Request Form (Onboarding Access Request) – template link: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change Request Template – /confluence/templates/change-request
- Vendor Request & Questionnaire – /confluence/templates/vendor-request
- Expense Report Template – /confluence/templates/expense-report
- Travel Itinerary & Emergency Contact Form – /confluence/templates/travel-itinerary

Enforcement and exceptions

- Exceptions to these policies must be submitted through the Policy Exception Request process and will be reviewed by the Policy Review Board (People Ops + Security + Finance).
- Approved exceptions are timeboxed and require compensating controls and quarterly revalidation.

Training and compliance

- All employees must complete annual security and data handling training.
- People Ops runs policy refresh sessions quarterly for managers.
- Failure to comply with critical controls (e.g., offboarding, DPA, breach reporting) may result in disciplinary action per HR policy.
